purpose: Wave C: the decision gate on whether the planet Places rebuild is worth paying for, and how to size head_result_cap.
verdict: REBUILD YES. HEAD CAP RAISE: NO -- ship the reorder at the existing cap of 10.

method.scope: 15 bbox-bounded metros (Paris, Seattle, Tokyo, Barcelona, Berlin, Sao Paulo, Lagos, New York, London, Rome, Monaco, Agra, Cusco, Sydney, San Francisco)
method.tokenizer: reimplemented; reproduces every hand vector in places_transform_v1.rs

fidelity_check.claim: head rows per token at cap 10
fidelity_check.note: not a fitted parameter -- this is the strongest evidence the simulation tracks the real pipeline

q1_which_key_level_decides.claim: The cap remains arbitrary a third of the time, and widening it makes that WORSE.
q1_which_key_level_decides.why_identity_looks_inert: It PRE-EMPTS the boundary rather than deciding it. Of contested tokens 92.0% are all-identifying, 2.0% all-context, 5.9% mixed -- and in 95.3% of the mixed ones identity alone already fills the top 10, so the boundary lands inside the identifying block. It is still what fixed the Monaco `monte` regression.

flat_default_reconciliation.wave_c_reported: Foursquare modal share 86.2% over a 6-metro mix, and attributed the softening to top-level `confidence` vs `sources[].confidence`
flat_default_reconciliation.that_attribution_is_WRONG: verified 2026-08-01 by direct query on the TOP-LEVEL confidence column
flat_default_reconciliation.actual_cause: US region mix. US metros are conflated, so including them softens the modal share. The claim in benchmarks/2026-08-01-confidence-and-duplicates.json -- exactly 0.7700 across six NON-US regions -- stands exactly as scoped.

q3_old_vs_new_cap.claim: The reorder is invisible on the routed path and decisive on the head path.

routed_path.mechanism: merge_routed_candidates AND-intersects but has a saturated-posting fallback -- a record missing from a saturated posting is still admitted if its own display fields carry the token
routed_path.the_2_failures: statue-of-liberty (with `new york`) and machu-picchu (with `cusco`) are context-field data gaps, identical in BOTH orderings
routed_path.consequence: if the routed path were the only consumer, this rebuild would not be worth paying for

head_path.mechanism: intersect_ranked, strict AND, NO fallback, hard-limited to tokens.len() <= 2
head_path.regression_mechanism: both match on a generic second token (`gate`, `museum`) via a common name, landing in a large identity+prominence-tied block where a low continuous meta confidence buries them. The cap raise rescues neither.
head_path.also: 14 of 25 POI gold cases have >2 tokens and the head path returns nothing at all regardless of cap; 10 of 35 gold cases expect a locality and are served by divisions, out of scope for this cap

q4_head_cap_10_to_64.decision: NOT DONE. Operator decision 2026-08-01: ship the reorder at cap 10.
q4_head_cap_10_to_64.not_6_4x_because: 69% of tokens have exactly one candidate; only 6.2% exceed 10 and 1.7% exceed 64
q4_head_cap_10_to_64.gold_gain: +2 of 11 (buckingham 14, big-ben 15), both in the 11-20 band -- a cap of ~24 buys them at 1.2-1.4x

head_wall_clock.verdict: at the central estimate the head phase does not fit in one job

duckdb_spill_share.verdict: UNQUANTIFIED -- the cap-10 run's actual peak temp usage is recorded nowhere

q4_head_cap_10_to_64.planet_scale_counterweight: required caps grow roughly as sqrt(n). Measured directly by widening from home-region-only to all 15 regions: eiffel 3->5, big-ben 6->15, buckingham 5->14, times 2->4, louvre 20->455, brandenburg 17->243. If planet postings for global tokens (tower, palace, museum, gate) are ~30x this union, cap 10 likely holds ~3/11 and cap 64 ~6/11 at planet scale. The ORDERING of the answer survives; the COUNTS probably do not.

q5_tied_groups_persist_and_scale.claim: The Monaco tied-group finding was not a small-slice artifact; it grows with metro size.

original_shape_remeasured.metric: (token, prominence) groups holding >10 tied NAME matches

q5_tied_groups_persist_and_scale.direct: 22,742 of 66,802 cap-10 boundaries (34.0%) fall inside a group tied all the way to the UUID

not_measured: Planet scale. 15 metros is 3-4% of the planet and required head caps are LOWER BOUNDS.
The DuckDB temp peak and head wall clock at cap 64 -- projected linearly from the cap-10 run, never executed.

Reimplementation divergence risk: Python str.lower() vs Rust char::to_lowercase differ on a few codepoints (e.g. Turkish dotted I); str.strip() vs str::trim trim different whitespace sets; NFKD comes from Python's table, not the compile-time-pinned unicode-normalization 17.0. All hand vectors pass, so any divergence is in the long tail.

source_object_index/row_group/row_index are pipeline-internal and absent from a direct S3 query -- they cannot change a result, because feature_id is already unique per record so the locator tail never fires between distinct records.
Serving-cap edge truncation: the 256 cap is per (partition_cell, token) on a 256x256 global grid, and the bboxes are smaller than one cell, so the 256 numbers are conservative.
taxonomy.primary is not read, matching project_places_construction_v1.py which passes None for it.

The gold 'expected feature' definition is the probe's own (alias-token subset within tolerance_km, filtered to exact name match OR prominence_rank > 0). A different alias list moves per-case numbers but not the 0->6 headline.

The probe counts 43 Eiffel records / 43 name-forms within 500 m against the ~87/53 reported at 12 km in benchmarks/2026-08-01-confidence-and-duplicates.json. Almost certainly a radius/criteria difference rather than a contradiction, but it was not reconciled.
